subject: Deal-linked buffer proposal & GPU cost exposure plan
messages:
From: Alex Torres <procurement@nebulaai.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Li <jordan@cloudops.vista.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@nebulaai.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved capacity - buffer sizing and exposure questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the call yesterday. We reviewed the draft term sheet and have two quick asks before we proceed to legal:

1) Can Redwood include a deal-linked buffer (10-15%) above the committed SKU so we can absorb spikes during our feature launches without exhausting burst capacity?
2) How will price movement in the GPU market affect the committed unit pricing — specifically: is there a floor/ceiling, and what approvals are required if Redwood needs to pass through a cost increase?

Jordan mentioned wanting a short "market-exposure" clause so procurement can model worst-case unit cost. Samir and I will need that language for our finance team.

Would appreciate a short note on options + recommended approach by EoD Wednesday (Dec 2).

Best,
Alex Torres
Head of Procurement, NebulaAI
[attachment: nebula_priority_launch_schedule.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Alex Torres <procurement@nebulaai.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity - buffer sizing and exposure questions

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Below is an operational proposal and three commercial paths we can offer. Short summary first, then details.

Summary (recommended): offer a tiered buffer (10% guaranteed, additional 10% burstable on best-effort with priority fallback) plus a price-exposure clause with a defined pass-through trigger tied to market index X. That balances availability for your launches and limits capital exposure for both sides.

Option A — Fixed buffer + fixed price (low friction)- 10% reserved buffer added to committed SKU, fixed per-unit price for the term. No GPU-pass-through except for extraordinary events (rare).

Option B — Tiered buffer + limited pass-through (recommended)- 10% guaranteed buffer; additional 10% burstable (no SLA). Pricing: per-unit price guaranteed up to GPU-spot-index level L1; above L1 we apply a shared pass-through: Redwood absorbs 50% of increase up to L2, beyond L2 Nebula absorbs incremental. Requires Finance & Sales approval chain.

Option C — Dynamic buffer + indexation (lower upfront price)- Buffer varies with quota utilization; unit price indexed to GPU market index with quarterly true-ups. Best for long tenors but more variability on Nebula side.

Operational notes:
- We can implement a canary routing rule to shift traffic to burst pools during launches.
- We'll deliver a capacity model spreadsheet showing cost exposure for each option (attached).

I'll loop in Vivek for the runtime/operational constraints and Karthik for approval path. Deliverable: updated term sheet language + modeled 3-year P&L by Thursday EoD.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | soojin_lee@redwood.com
[attachment: reserve_capacity_buffer_model.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity - buffer sizing and exposure questions

Adding implementation constraints and a recommended control for the recommended Option B.

Implementation constraints:
- Guaranteed buffer requires pinned SKUs in the Dedicated pool; we need to reserve capacity at least 12 weeks ahead to ensure availability for Q1 launches.
- Burstable capacity will live in a preemptible/overflow pool; we can provision an autoscaler rule but cannot guarantee latency SLAs for that tier.

Control & failover suggestion:
- Canary rule: when a launch is detected, route 20% of traffic to burst pool for 5 minutes, measure latency & error rates; if within thresholds, slowly ramp to full burst allowance. If not, fallback to a smaller model variant automatically.

Cost exposure model (high level):
- If GPU spot index increases by <= 12%: Redwood absorbs (to maintain partner experience) for the first 6 months, then shared pass-through kicks in per Option B.
- If index spikes > 25%: automatic trigger to executive review (Finance + Sales) for temporary surcharge and capacity rebalancing.

I recommend we include an explicit executive-approval ladder in the term sheet:
- Finance Manager (Mina) approves up to +8% pass-through
- Head of Sales (Karthik) approves up to +15%
- COO/Exec (> +15%) requires CEO sign-off

Vivek
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Torres <procurement@nebulaai.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@nebulaai.com>, Jordan Li <jordan@cloudops.vista.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:48:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity - buffer sizing and exposure questions

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from finance:

• Can we get hard language for a price-exposure floor so Nebula is protected from sudden surcharges in the first 9 months?
• For the guaranteed 10% buffer, will Redwood guarantee placement on specific GPU types (A100 vs newer) or just equivalent performance? We need to avoid quiet substitutions that affect model performance.

On the approval ladder: Nebula is comfortable with Finance Manager approval up to +6% but wants a cap at +12% without an explicit bilateral re-negotiation. Above 12% we'd expect a re-opener.

Attached our preferred clause markup and a quick schedule for our January launch.

Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Procurement, NebulaAI

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 14:09:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity - buffer sizing and exposure questions

Team — aligning on a response and what we can commit to commercially. My notes and ask for approvals: 

1) Buffer guarantee: agree to guaranteed 10% on the same GPU class; require a 90-day lead to secure pinned capacity. Legal will add language preventing silent downgrades (Olga).
2) Price exposure floor: propose Redwood guarantees no pass-through for the first 9 months (protects Nebula), then a soft cap mechanism: pass-through allowed up to +12% over baseline; beyond that either party can trigger a re-opener. Mina: please confirm finance comfortability with absorbing up to +6% for the first quarter before escalating to our customer-sharing formula.
3) Approval ladder: approved as Vivek suggested, but we will codify thresholds as % deltas in the term sheet and require exec notification timestamps (48 hours).

Attachments: draft approval memo for signoff. Requesting Mina to sign off on the +6% pre-absorb and Olga to confirm legal language on silent substitution and re-opener clause. If approved, I'll prepare the DocuSign for Nebula.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Olga — please confirm legal language around GPU-class parity (no surprise substitutions) and the re-opener process. Once we have that, Soojin — please proceed to send the final term sheet and DocuSign link to Nebula.
